correctness.rationale: For \(f=a\delta_0+b\delta_s\), each time slice is a two-term character polynomial. The character \(\xi\mapsto\omega^{-s\xi}\) has image size \(N/d\) and fibers of size \(d\), so a slice has either zero or exactly \(d\) zeros. Excluding the finite collection of algebraic equalities between the root cosets \(-\overline{g(j+s)}/\overline{g(j)}\,\mu_{N/d}\), together with coordinate hyperplanes, gives a nonempty Zariski-open set on which a coefficient ratio can hit at most one time slice. Both zero counts are attainable. The ordinary two-point Fourier polynomial has the identical \(d\)-zero alternative, proving the shifted support spectra. As \(s\) varies, \(d\) runs through the proper divisors of \(N\), and the largest is \(N/p\). The universal upper bound on \(\phi\) follows from a singleton when the window has a zero, or from forcing one \(N/p\)-zero slice when it has full support. I independently checked the distinct-ratio and character-fiber arithmetic for every \(2\le N\le120\) and all nonzero differences.

value.rationale: This resolves a complete nontrivial stratum of an explicit cyclic Gabor uncertainty question, for every composite and prime order, and gives the exact generic support-at-most-two optimum. The gcd formula also explains earlier numerical data and is a natural reusable sparse-signal invariant.

final_claim: For every \(N\ge2\), a nonempty Zariski-open set of cyclic Gabor windows has the exact two-sparse support correspondence: for a fixed support difference \(s\), with \(d=\gcd(N,s)\), the attainable STFT support sizes are \(\{N^2,N^2-d\}\) and the ordinary Fourier support sizes are \(\{N,N-d\}\); consequently \(\phi(\mathbb Z_N,2)=N^2-N/p\) for the least prime divisor \(p\) of \(N\).
limitations: Exact signal-support size two, plus the derived support-at-most-two optimum, only.
The theorem does not settle the full cyclic support-pair correspondence for support sizes three through \(N\) or characterize all exceptional windows.
